sections.h2: What should a Warren homeowner know before selling a house?
sections.html:
Three local pieces shape a Warren sale: a few Building Division and rental rules, the Macomb County recording office in Mount Clemens, and a tax calendar that splits between city and county. Warren is Macomb County's biggest community and the state's third-largest city, so title agents and inspectors here run through these items all the time.

Accepting a cash offer on an as-is basis skips the showings and the repair list. It does nothing to the recording step, the seller's transfer tax, or any city bill still attached to the parcel. The headings below follow the order in which a seller usually runs into each one.

sections.h2: What is Warren like as a place to own a house?
sections.html:
Warren occupies a six-by-six mile square at the southwest tip of Macomb County, between 8 Mile Road and 14 Mile Road, and it wraps around the small city of Center Line. The city is 34.4 square miles, and its entire southern edge touches Detroit. Beebe's Corners, the first settlement, began in 1830 at Mound Road and Chicago Road. Voters made Warren a city on January 1, 1957.

Growth came fast: 42,653 people in 1950, then 179,260 by 1970, fed by the Detroit Arsenal Tank Plant, a Chrysler truck plant and the General Motors Technical Center. Southeast Warren has many bungalows from the years right after World War II. North of Stephens Road, a lot of the housing is brick ranches from after 1960.

  • Southeast Warren takes in Warrendale, Belangers Garden, Berkshire Manor and Piper Van Dyke.
  • Southwest Warren holds Fitzgerald and Beierman Farms.
  • Northeast Warren includes Bear Creek, Bella Vista Estates, Fairlane Estates and downtown.
  • Northwest Warren is mostly the west half of Warren Con.

Cold matters for a house of this age. NOAA normals show about 39 days a year when Warren never climbs above freezing, so a buyer's inspector will look hard at the furnace, roof and pipes.

sections.h2: Who employs Warren residents, and how do the roads connect them?
sections.html:
According to the city's 2022 financial report, General Motors employs 23,823 people in Warren. The federal government is next at 7,800, tied to the Detroit Arsenal. Stellantis has 5,523, Ascension Health 2,407 and Lipari Foods 1,300. Steady payrolls like these keep a pool of local buyers in the market.

I-696 runs east and west across the city. Van Dyke Avenue (M-53) divides it north from south, Groesbeck Highway (M-97) angles through the southeast corner, and Mound Road is a second major north-south route. SMART runs the buses. Warren workers spend a mean of 24.9 minutes getting to work, per the Census Bureau.

Macomb Intermediate School District oversees the six public districts that serve Warren, and Macomb Community College keeps a campus here. District lines wind through neighborhoods, so check the district tied to a particular address instead of trusting a street name.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Warren housing?
sections.html:
Warren's estimated population for July 1, 2025 is 137,138, which sits 1.6 percent below the April 2020 base. From 2020 through 2024 the Census counted 54,744 households of roughly 2.5 people, and 71.1 percent of them owned their home.

Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $193,400. Renters pay a median gross rent of $1,225, and the median household income is $64,016. Typical monthly owner costs are $1,403 for those with a mortgage and $557 for those without. A single block can look quite different from any of these citywide numbers.

sections.h2: Which Warren city rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Warren's residential city certification, as the posted application describes it, covers a vacant dwelling that has been posted "no occupancy": nobody may move in until the Building Division confirms the house meets the International Property Maintenance Code and the zoning ordinance. The office is at One City Square, Suite 305 (586-574-4504).

Rental owners face more. The rental ordinance posted by the Rental Inspections Division sets these terms:

  • No one may rent or occupy a rental dwelling without a rental license, and licenses do not transfer between landlords or units.
  • A license lasts two years and needs a biennial inspection.
  • Sale of the property ends the license immediately.
  • No license is issued until prior property taxes, special assessments, water or sewer bills and mowing or cleanup charges are paid.

If tenants live in the house, call the Rental Inspections Division at 586-574-4633 and find out where the license stands before you list. Open balances there are easy to miss.

The same Building Division enforces the Michigan Building Code and Michigan Residential Code, which every Michigan community has had to adopt since 2004, along with Warren's zoning ordinance. A sunroom, deck or finished basement built without a permit is the kind of item that surfaces during a buyer's walkthrough, so gather permit records for past work early.

sections.h2: Where does a Warren deed get recorded, and what are the charges?
sections.html:
Warren lies in Macomb County, so the deed is filed with the county Register of Deeds at 120 N. Main St. in Mount Clemens (phone 586-469-7953). Counter hours run weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4:15 p.m. A flat per-document fee has applied since October 1, 2016, whatever the page count.

Macomb County recording charges. Source: Macomb County Register of Deeds recording fee and transfer tax pages.
ItemCharge
Deed, mortgage or other instrument$30 per document
Document assigning or discharging several instruments$3 added for each extra instrument
Tax certificate (warranty deeds, land contracts)$5 for up to five legal descriptions
State transfer taxSale price multiplied by .0075
Macomb County transfer taxSale price multiplied by .0011

Before a warranty deed or land contract is accepted, it needs a tax certificate from the county treasurer. The seller carries the transfer tax. Macomb publishes a schedule in $500 steps for anyone who wants the exact figure for a price.

sections.h2: When are Warren property taxes due?
sections.html:
The City of Warren sends summer bills (city and school) in early July and winter bills (county) in early December. The dates below come from the Treasurer's tax payment page; the Treasurer's Office at 586-574-4542 can confirm them for the current year.

  • Pay the summer bill whole, or split it by paying the first half by August 31. The second half is billed December 1 and due January 31.
  • From September 1 only the entire summer balance is taken, with a 1 percent fee that month and half a percent for every month after.
  • The winter bill is payable December 1 through February 28.
  • A balance still open after February 28 goes to the Macomb County Treasurer, with a further 4 percent fee and 1 percent interest monthly.

Ask your title agent how these will be divided at closing. An unpaid bill can hold up a rental license or a clear title, so call the Treasurer's Office before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Do I need a city inspection to sell my Warren house?
faqs.a: The city certification on Warren's posted application covers vacant houses marked no occupancy, which must pass a Building Division inspection before anyone moves in. Phone 586-574-4504 to learn whether your parcel carries that posting.

faqs.q: What happens to a Warren rental license when the property sells?
faqs.a: It ends at once. The rental ordinance says a sale terminates the license and that licenses cannot move between owners. The new owner applies again and the unit is inspected afresh.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when a Warren house sells?
faqs.a: The seller does. Macomb County prints the state rate as .0075 times the sale price and the county rate as .0011 times the sale price, and both are collected at recording.

faqs.q: Which office records the deed on a Warren sale?
faqs.a: The Macomb County Register of Deeds in Mount Clemens. The fee is $30 for the document, and a warranty deed first needs a tax certificate from the county treasurer.

faqs.q: What if I am behind on Warren property taxes before a sale?
faqs.a: Pay the Warren Treasurer's Office before the winter bill's February 28 cutoff. After that the balance moves to the Macomb County Treasurer with added fees and monthly interest, so clear it or have the title agent include it in the payoff.
